subject: Legend with one element is too big

messages.author: ecfd01ab625972da
messages.subject: Legend with one element is too big
parts:
If a legend contains two or more elements, then its border fits snugly
around its contents.

two_groups <- data.frame(
x = rep.int(1:10, 2),
y = runif(20),
g = factor(rep(letters[1:2], each = 10))
)

p_two_groups <- ggplot(two_groups, aes(x, y, shape = g)) +
geom_point() +
opts(legend.background = theme_rect(colour = "red"))
p_two_groups

By contrast, if there is only one element within the legend then the
border is too tall.

one_group <- data.frame(
x = 1:10,
y = runif(10),
g = factor(rep("a", each = 10))
)

p_one_group <- p_two_groups %+% one_group
p_one_group

I presume that this is a bug rather than deliberate behaviour but I'm
not sure where to look to fix it. Is there a way to manually override
the legend size in this case?

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Legend with one element is too big
parts:
I tried hunting down the bug and found where the height is computed,
and traced the bug back to a bug in grid::unit.pmax. I've filed a bug
report on that. https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla3/show_bug.cgi?id=14443

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

patched." according to Brian Ripley. The fix was in revision 53664,
so any patched build after that should have it.
